data.raw_text:
Ahrefs redirected the entire 1M+ organic traffic folder with reports by specific websites to a separate domain a week ago.

They redirected ahrefs[.]com/websites/ to ahrefstop[.]com/websites/

I am glad they confirmed my hypothesis. 

I thought about creating and indexing similar reports at Sitechecker 4 years ago, but I rejected it. I saw how Woorank did it, then Seobility, then even Semrush.

However, I felt that something was wrong with it. It's easy to recognize what's wrong if you go deep enough. 2 things matter:

1/ Almost 0 conversion potential of such content.

Most of the people who find these reports are consumers who look for a specific brand on Google, just to visit the official website. They won't buy your software. 

2/ Big damage to the topical authority of the website.

If you have 1mln traffic about SEO and digital marketing, and then add 1mln traffic about everything else, you'll create a huge risk for existing content. If you're SaaS, don't pretend to be a media in Google's eyes. 

By the way, check the top countries by traffic, the Ahrefs' subfolder had: India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Philippines. These are some of the most populated countries, and of course, people look for specific websites there more than in other countries.

Marcos Jr.’s Taiwan Strait Blunder, Akin to Volunteering the Philippines for Someone Else’s War???
By Anna Malindog-Uy

Marcos Jr.’s retort, “Playing with fire? I was just stating facts,” might sound defiant on the surface, but in the realm of international law, Philippine foreign policy commitments, and even his own government’s records, it’s logically incoherent and politically reckless.

The One China Policy isn’t a matter of “subjective opinion or “alternative facts.” It is an established, documented, and binding framework for Philippine diplomacy. The Philippines formally recognized the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal government of China in 1975, under President Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr., with diplomatic relations established on that basis. This is not just a handshake agreement; it is enshrined in official treaties and agreements. For instance, the Joint Communiqué of June 9, 1975, clearly affirms Manila’s recognition of the PRC as the only China, with Taiwan considered an inalienable part of Chinese territory.
